source.publication: 2025 Form CT-1040 Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and Form CT-1040
source.section: PDF page 10, Line 48b; PDF page 24, Pension and Annuity Worksheet Line 1 '*' note (under 75,000: subtract 75% of Line 4b); PDF pages 19-23, Tax Calculation Schedule Lines 1-10 with Table A, Table B, Tables C-D and Table E; Form CT-1040 Lines 1-6

worked: Federal AGI = wages 40,000.00 + IRA distributions 20,000.00 = 60,000.00. Federal taxable income = 60,000.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65+ = 42,250.00 (given, not tested; federal senior deduction ignored). CT-1040 Line 1 federal AGI 60,000.00; Line 2 additions 0.00 (Schedule 1 Lines 31-37: none apply); Line 3 = 60,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 48b IRA (worksheet Line 2: 75% of Line 4b): 20,000.00 x 0.75 = 15,000.00; federal AGI 60,000.00 is under the 75,000.00 test, decimal 1; 15,000.00 x 1 = 15,000.00 -> 15,000.00. Schedule 1 Line 50 total subtractions = 15,000.00; CT-1040 Line 4 = 15,000.00. CT-1040 Line 5 Connecticut AGI = 60,000.00 - 15,000.00 = 45,000.00. Tax Calculation Schedule Line 1 = 45,000.00; Line 2 Table A: Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is more than 44,000.00, exemption 0.00; Line 3 taxable income = 45,000.00 - 0.00 = 45,000.00. Line 4 Table B (Single or Married Filing Separately schedule) on 45,000.00: 10,000.00 x 0.02 + 35,000.00 x 0.045 = 200.00 + 1,575.00 = 1,775.00. Line 5 Table C 0.00 (Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is not more than 56,500.00); Line 6 Table D 0.00 (not more than 105,000.00); Line 7 = 1,775.00. Line 8 Table E decimal 0.10 (Connecticut AGI 45,000.00 is in the band more than 33,300.00); Line 9 = 1,775.00 x 0.10 = 177.50. Line 10 Connecticut income tax = 1,775.00 - 177.50 = 1,597.50 (CT-1040 Line 6). No other credits (property tax credit not claimed: no property tax in the inputs, and not modelled). Note: Below the 75,000 test the worksheet is not completed; the '*' note subtracts 75% of the Line 4b IRA amount. The 15,000 subtraction lifts Connecticut AGI to 45,000, past the end of the single exemption phase-out.
